data.long_meaning: Aylward is an Anglo-Saxon name derived from the Old English elements æl (noble) and weard (guard). It was commonly given to boys born into noble families and meant 'noble warrior'. The name Aylward carries the meaning “Noble and brave” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Aylward usually hope their child will grow to embody noble and brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Its meaning as 'noble warrior' represented a revered social status and a courageous identity, often associated with the valor and chivalry of the nobility during that time. As such, its significance can be seen in the many knights and warriors of legend and history who bore the name, embodying its ideals and contributing to the formation of a strong, proud and warlike society.
